name: shell-hygiene
description: Blocks shell commands that reach past what the agent started or created: processes by pattern, and machine-wide installs, prunes, services and settings; and common numeric `chmod` modes, and commands that print a secret into the session: `op read`, `op item get --reveal`, `gh auth token`, `gh auth status --show-token`, `gh config get oauth_token`, `security find-generic-password -w`, `secretspec run -- env` and every `secretspec run -- op ...`. `op read` and `op item --reveal` are version 1 rules because a version 1 subcommand skips an `op` global option such as `--account my`, which a version 2 command path doesn't. `secretspec run -- op` is blocked whatever `op` does, since a rule can't require two arguments together and `secretspec` is not a transparent wrapper. The shell-hygiene-secrets rulebook holds the other `op` rules and the `nix run` rule. With `nix` in the config's `transparent_wrappers`, these rules also block their commands run through `nix develop --command` or `nix shell`. Complements CC Safety Net's built-in rm and find rules. The why and the alternatives live in the shell-hygiene-* skills in nhooey/shell-skills. A rule whose block_args holds the command's own name blocks every call to it. Gaps: `sudo` is analyzed as a wrapper and can't be blocked here, `kill $(pgrep -f ...)` isn't caught, and `rm -rf "$DIR"/` with an empty variable is left to the skill. Not caught: a bare `secretspec get`, `script ... op read`, `secretspec run -- sh -c 'op read ...'` or `secretspec run -- sh -c 'echo ...'`.
author: nhooey/shell-skills

rules.name: pkill
rules.reason: Matches every process whose name or command line contains the pattern, the agent's own shell included. Kill the PID you started: `kill <pid>`.

rules.name: killall
rules.reason: Stops every process with that name in every session. Kill the PID you started: `kill <pid>`.

rules.name: xargs-kill
rules.reason: Kills whatever a search matched, such as whatever holds a port. Look with `lsof -i :<port>` or `pgrep -l`, then `kill <pid>` for your own process.

rules.name: rsync-delete
rules.reason: Deletes every file in the destination that isn't in the source. Sync into a fresh directory, or ask the user after showing them `rsync -n --delete`'s list.

rules.name: chmod-recursive
rules.reason: Changes permissions on a whole tree. Change the one file that needs it.

rules.name: chown-recursive
rules.reason: Changes ownership of a whole tree. Change the one file that needs it.

rules.name: brew-machine-wide
rules.reason: Changes Homebrew tools every project uses. Use the project's dev shell or `nix shell`, or ask the user.

rules.name: brew-services
rules.reason: Changes services for every session. Run the service in the foreground for the task.

rules.name: npm-global
rules.reason: Changes global npm packages or config. Use `npx` or the project's dependencies.

rules.name: nix-collect-garbage
rules.reason: Deletes store paths other projects and sessions use. Leave garbage collection to the user.

rules.name: nix-store-gc
rules.reason: Deletes store paths other projects and sessions use. Leave garbage collection to the user.

rules.name: docker-prune
rules.reason: Removes every unused container, image, volume or network, not just yours. Remove the ones you started, by id.

rules.name: launchctl-change
rules.reason: Changes launchd services for every session. Run the process in the foreground for the task, or ask the user.

rules.name: systemctl-change
rules.reason: Changes systemd services for every session. Run the process in the foreground for the task, or ask the user.

rules.name: defaults-write
rules.reason: Changes macOS settings for every program. Ask the user, or put the setting in their declarative config.

rules.name: chmod-numeric
rules.reason: A number resets every permission bit. Write the change you mean as a symbolic mode: `u+x` or `go-w`, or `=` for an exact mode, such as `u=rwx,go=rx` for 755, `u=rw,go=r` for 644 or `u=rw,go=` for 600.

rules.name: op-read
rules.reason: Prints a secret into the session. Read it through SecretSpec into the one command that needs it: `secretspec get --reason "…" KEY`.

rules.name: op-item-reveal
rules.reason: Prints a concealed field or a one-time code into the session. Read it through SecretSpec: `secretspec get --reason "…" KEY`. `op item get <id> --fields <field>` still shows a field that isn't concealed.

rules.name: gh-auth-token
rules.reason: Prints the user's GitHub token into the session, as `gh auth token` and `gh auth status --show-token` do. `gh` uses it without printing it; a command that needs a token reads one through SecretSpec: `secretspec get --reason "…" GITHUB_TOKEN`.

rules.name: gh-config-token
rules.reason: Prints the user's GitHub token where `gh` keeps it in its config file. `gh` uses it without printing it; a command that needs a token reads one through SecretSpec: `secretspec get --reason "…" GITHUB_TOKEN`.

rules.name: security-print-password
rules.reason: Prints a keychain password into the session. Read it through SecretSpec into the one command that needs it: `secretspec get --reason "…" KEY`.

rules.name: secretspec-run-print
rules.reason: Prints every secret `secretspec run` loaded into the session. Run the command that needs them instead.

rules.name: secretspec-run-op
rules.reason: Runs `op` with SecretSpec's access, where `op read`, `op item get --reveal` or `--format json` print a secret into the session. Let SecretSpec read the secret into the command that needs it: `secretspec run --reason "…" -- <command>`.

tests.command: secretspec get --reason "deploy: push the release tag" GITHUB_TOKEN
secretspec run --reason "read the token" -- op item get abc --reveal
secretspec run --profile deploy -- op item get abc --format json
secretspec run -- op --account my item get abc --format=JSON
secretspec run -- op document get abc
nix develop --command secretspec run -- op read op://vault/item/field
secretspec run --reason "deploy: push the release tag" -- git push --tags
secretspec run --reason "publish the image" -- docker push ghcr.io/nhooey/app
GITHUB_TOKEN="$(secretspec get --reason "deploy: push the release tag" GITHUB_TOKEN)" gh api user
